headline: The US Department of Energy has released a free package of guidance and workflows to help scientists use AI coding tools in research.
score_reason: Lowered by 1: the DOE announcement was on 15 Oct 2026, a day before the window; official release but modest and no results reported.
importance_line: Scientists and developers can use shared national-laboratory guidance for AI-assisted research free of charge, though it is a new release with no reported results yet on how well it works.
summary: ExecutiveGov reports that the US Department of Energy said on Thursday 15 Oct 2026 it has published Genesis Agent Skills, a free package on GitLab that lets researchers ask AI coding tools for technical guidance or code reviews based on guidance from the Genesis Mission, the DOE programme linking national laboratories, industry and academia to apply AI to science. It is the first package from DOE's ModCon effort and covers AI safety, agent evaluation and monitoring, data governance and multi-agent systems.
notes: Read in full from ExecutiveGov. The DOE statement was on Thursday 15 Oct 2026; ExecutiveGov published on 16 Oct 2026.
